def-additive-ode-and-partition.conclusion: This Definition names a split a+b and an initial-value problem; it asserts neither existence of subflows nor solvability of implicit stages.
def-additive-ode-and-partition.empty: The initial state y0 is supplied in the open set U and d>=1; an empty U cannot supply such input.
def-additive-ode-and-partition.nonempty-choice: The split fields and initial state are given data; the Definition explicitly avoids selecting any unsupplied exact subflow or implicit-stage solution.
def-additive-ode-and-partition.degenerate: The two fields may vanish or be equal; no invertibility or nonzero bracket is needed to define a+b, and no existence theorem for their flows is claimed.
def-additive-ode-and-partition.one: The Definition admits d=1, where the displayed equation is the scalar sum y'=a(y)+b(y); no multidimensional rank assumption is used.
def-additive-ode-and-partition.endpoints: This autonomous IVP Definition has a supplied initial time t0, not a closed interval of step parameters or an endpoint error estimate.
def-additive-ode-and-partition.zero: The state value y0=0 is allowed when0 lies in U; zero dimension is excluded by d>=1, and no quotient by the initial state occurs.

def-dirichlet-sine-mode-heat-splitting-m.conclusion: The Definition constructs fixed diagonal and translation subflows on sequence space, with no converse domain or general PDE convergence assertion.
def-dirichlet-sine-mode-heat-splitting-m.nonempty-choice: The forcing coordinates g_k and both subflows are explicitly specified for every k>=1; no eigenbasis or unspecified state is selected.
def-dirichlet-sine-mode-heat-splitting-m.degenerate: Even modal forcing coefficients are zero by definition. E_t and B_t are still defined there, with translation zero on each even coordinate.
def-dirichlet-sine-mode-heat-splitting-m.one: The modal model retains all k>=1; selecting only one mode would be a separate finite truncation, not another parameter value of the defined sequence space.

alg-imex-euler-step.conclusion: The algorithm returns a residual-checked candidate or a declared failure status; it makes no converse existence certificate from arbitrary solver output.
alg-imex-euler-step.empty: An admissible input supplies y in U and a closed ball centered at c=y+ha(y); the center belongs to its ball, so neither the state domain nor the selected ball is empty.
alg-imex-euler-step.nonempty-choice: The solve routine is supplied and may return a failure; procedure1 returns solver-unavailable when absent. The algorithm never silently selects a root.
alg-imex-euler-step.degenerate: checked|Definition procedure2 returns branch-not-certified when hLb>=1 or the invariance bound fails; a solver failure is propagated in procedure4. No singular branch is accepted merely as a root.
alg-imex-euler-step.one: For d=1 the same displayed scalar residual and closed-ball membership tests apply; the algorithm uses no determinant or factorization whose size must exceed one.

def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.conclusion: The Definition fixes composition order and bracket Db a-Da b on admitted local-flow intervals; it asserts no converse solvability or unbounded-operator claim.
def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.empty: It restricts to supplied points and intervals for which the unique subflows remain in U; an empty admissible set yields no chosen starting point or claimed trajectory.
def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.nonempty-choice: The subflows are the assumed unique local solution maps; the Lie and Strang maps are explicit finite compositions, not selections among multiple roots.
def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.degenerate: If a or b is zero or the bracket vanishes, the same composition/bracket formulas remain defined; the Definition makes no nonzero-error assertion.
def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.one: Scalar fields in d=1 use the same compositions and ordinary derivatives in Db a-Da b; the definition is not restricted to noncommuting matrix fields.
def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.endpoints: The composition maps are defined only on their admitted local time intervals; no assertion extends them through an interval where a subflow leaves U.
def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bra.zero: At time0 each exact solution map is the identity by its initial condition, so the Lie and Strang zero-time compositions are identity; no quotient by h is part of this Definition.

lem-diagonal-heat-semigroup-generator-do.conclusion: The generator-domain identification is a true equivalence between existence of the right norm derivative and weighted square summability.
lem-diagonal-heat-semigroup-generator-do.iff-forward: checked|Proof3.1 assumes the right generator limit exists in H, uses continuity of each coordinate evaluation to identify v_k=-k^2u_k, then sums |v_k|^2 to prove u belongs to D(A).
lem-diagonal-heat-semigroup-generator-do.iff-reverse: checked|Proof1.2 assumes u belongs to D(A), bounds the squared difference-quotient tail by4 times the weighted square-sum tail, and combines it with finite-head coordinate limits to obtain the right norm derivative Au.
lem-diagonal-heat-semigroup-generator-do.nonempty-choice: Proof2.1 chooses a finite tail cutoff from the convergence of the supplied square sum; it does not select vectors from an empty modal set.
lem-diagonal-heat-semigroup-generator-do.degenerate: checked|The zero sequence has E_t0=0 and generator derivative0; all head/tail bounds in proof1.2 and2.1 vanish, without dividing by its norm.
lem-diagonal-heat-semigroup-generator-do.one: The Statement concerns the full sequence space with fixed index set k>=1; one retained coordinate is a permissible finite-support vector, and proof1.2 has a zero tail after that coordinate.

lem-imex-euler-local-branch.conclusion: Invariant-ball and contraction bounds imply one selected local root and a residual-error estimate, not a converse global-root criterion.
lem-imex-euler-local-branch.empty: checked|Proof1.1 explicitly places c in the closed ball and proves its completeness before applying the fixed-point theorem.
lem-imex-euler-local-branch.nonempty-choice: checked|Proof2.1 obtains the unique root from the contraction theorem on the nonempty complete ball established in proof1.1, rather than choosing an unspecified root.
lem-imex-euler-local-branch.degenerate: The hypotheses R>0 and hL<1 retain a positive residual denominator1-hL in proof3.1. L=0 is allowed and makes the selected map constant, with denominator1.
lem-imex-euler-local-branch.one: For scalar dimension1, proof1.1 gives a closed interval and proof1.2 the same hL contraction; the proof uses Euclidean completeness and norms, not higher-dimensional geometry.

def-ars222-additive-tableau-and-stages.conclusion: The Definition specifies the fixed three-stage ARS222 tableau and staged equations; it does not characterize all second-order additive methods.
def-ars222-additive-tableau-and-stages.empty: The tableau has exactly three indexed stages, with Y1=y; it does not take an arbitrary possibly empty stage list.
def-ars222-additive-tableau-and-stages.nonempty-choice: The Definition selects roots in their specified branch balls and may report failure; numerical stage existence is delegated to the named local-branch result, not assumed for arbitrary equations.
def-ars222-additive-tableau-and-stages.degenerate: The first implicit tableau row is zero and its first stage is explicitly Y1=y; the later two diagonal entries are the positive constant gamma, not a rank assumption on a full tableau.
def-ars222-additive-tableau-and-stages.one: Scalar dimension1 is admitted for each stage vector; it does not reduce the fixed three-stage tableau to a one-stage method.
def-ars222-additive-tableau-and-stages.endpoints: The abscissae are fixed0,gamma,1; stages at the initial and final time are part of the stated equations, not limits of a free tableau parameter.

lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.conclusion: Admitted C3 finite-dimensional flows give Lie and Strang defect expansions; vanishing brackets are permitted and no converse recovery of smoothness is claimed.
lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.empty: If K0 is empty the uniform pointwise assertions have no input y; the proof begins at a supplied y in K0 and does not infer a trajectory from emptiness.
lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.nonempty-choice: Proof1.1 works with the assumed exact subflows at a supplied starting point and each fixed coordinate function; no unspecified solution branch is chosen.
lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.degenerate: checked|If the bracket or nested brackets vanish, the coefficients derived in proof3.1 and4.1 are zero; the stated O(h^3) and o(h^3) remainders do not assert nonzero leading errors.
lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.one: Proof1.1 expands each scalar coordinate; when d=1 there is exactly one coordinate expansion and the bracket calculation in proof3.1 remains valid.
lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.endpoints: The Statement restricts to sufficiently small positive h whose full compositions remain in K; no error estimate beyond the admitted flow interval is asserted.
lem-lie-strang-local-error-expansions.zero: The defect expansions are asymptotics as h tends to zero through positive steps; proof1.1 expands exact flows about time0 and never evaluates a quotient at h=0.

lem-dirichlet-forcing-coefficients-excee.conclusion: The fixed constant forcing has the specified sine coefficients, belongs to H and fails the generator-domain condition; no converse for arbitrary boundary data is asserted.
lem-dirichlet-forcing-coefficients-excee.empty: The coefficient index set is all positive integers; proof2.2 uses infinitely many odd indices, so its divergent weighted sum is not an empty family.
lem-dirichlet-forcing-coefficients-excee.nonempty-choice: Proof1.1 computes each Fourier coefficient from an explicit integral and proof2.2 uses the explicit odd subsequence; there is no unspecified selection of a mode.
lem-dirichlet-forcing-coefficients-excee.degenerate: Even coefficients vanish while every odd coefficient1/k is nonzero, so proof2.1 proves square summability and proof2.2 still obtains divergent generator weight.
lem-dirichlet-forcing-coefficients-excee.one: Proof1.1 includes the first mode k=1 with coefficient1; the conclusion about failure of D(A) uses the whole odd sequence rather than a single retained mode.

thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.conclusion: Common-tube, local-branch and small-step hypotheses imply defect O(h^2) and one-step stability; those bounds do not assert global branch existence.
thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.empty: The Statement supplies an exact solution, exact endpoint and selected branch root in the common tube; these points witness nonemptiness where the proof compares them.
thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.nonempty-choice: Proof2.1 compares the selected branch root supplied by the local-branch lemma with the admitted exact endpoint; no remote root is selected.
thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.degenerate: checked|When either Lipschitz constant vanishes, proof3.1 still bounds the ratio(1+hLa)/(1-hLb); the hypothesis hLb<=1/2 keeps its denominator at least1/2.
thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.one: The proof bounds Euclidean differences using the integral equation and Lipschitz inequalities; with d=1 these are scalar absolute-value inequalities with the same constants.
thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.endpoints: checked|Proof3.1 includes equality hLb=1/2 and still gives the stated factor1+2(La+Lb)h; no branch at hLb=1 is asserted.
thm-imex-euler-local-order-and-stability.zero: The local theorem assumes h>0; zero field bounds are allowed and make the corresponding integral estimates zero. No division by the value of y or of the field occurs.

lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.conclusion: The four identities hold for the single fixed gamma=1-1/sqrt2 and delta=-1/sqrt2; no family of equivalent tableaus is asserted.
lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.empty: The claim is an identity among two fixed real constants, not a sum or construction indexed by a stage family.
lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.nonempty-choice: sqrt2 is the specified positive square root; proof1.1 establishes it exceeds1 before reciprocals are used, without selecting from unspecified roots.
lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.degenerate: checked|Proof1.1 proves sqrt2>1 and gamma>0, so proof2.1 divides only by nonzero2gamma and2sqrt2(sqrt2-1).
lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.one: The constants are not a dimension or cardinality parameter; assigning gamma=1 would change the specified ARS222 tableau and is outside this identity.
lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.endpoints: gamma and delta are fixed constants rather than variables in a closed interval; the proof has no limiting parameter endpoint.
lem-ars222-coefficient-identities.zero: checked|Proof1.1 proves gamma>0 and sqrt2>1; proof2.1 consequently uses no zero denominator in the reciprocal identity.

lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.conclusion: Each of two sequential selected stage balls gives a unique local root and residual control; no remote or large-step root criterion is asserted.
lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.empty: Each closed stage ball contains its center; the second center is fixed after selecting the previous stage, as proof3.1 explicitly records.
lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.nonempty-choice: checked|Proof1.1 obtains the second stage by the local-branch supplier, and proof2.1 obtains the third stage only after its center is fixed; uniqueness prevents an arbitrary root choice.
lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.degenerate: The contraction hypothesis |gamma|hL<1 excludes a zero residual denominator. L=0 is allowed and makes the stage equation a constant-map fixed-point problem.
lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.one: The proof applies a one-stage matrix[gamma] separately to each implicit equation, including scalar state dimension1; it is already a one-block branch argument.
lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.endpoints: Equality |gamma|hM=R_j is allowed in the invariant-ball hypothesis, whereas the contraction inequality is strict. Proof1.1 and2.1 apply those exact inequalities.
lem-ars222-stage-branch-and-residual-con.zero: h>0 and gamma>0, while M=0 or L=0 remain permitted; the bound1-|gamma|hL then stays positive, including denominator1 at L=0.

thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.conclusion: Local splitting defects plus common-tube stability and appropriate subflow error budgets imply fixed-time orders1 and2; local subflow accuracy alone is not a converse stability certificate.
thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.empty: The Statement supplies an exact path and numerical states on[0,T]; it sums over a fixed N-step grid rather than arbitrary empty time data.
thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.nonempty-choice: The exact and approximate subflow maps are supplied on the tube; proof2.2 inserts those actual maps and does not choose unproved approximate solutions.
thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.degenerate: checked|Proof2.1 explicitly sets the stability constant to0 when K=La+Lb=0. Vanishing defect coefficients only improve the stated upper bounds.
thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.one: For N=1 the same local defect and stability bounds used in proof3.1 give the fixed-time estimate directly; no recurrence needs an interior time node.
thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.endpoints: Proof3.1 uses exact initial data and a fixed grid throughT. The approximate-subflow branch in proof4.1 assumes its own stability on the same admitted tube through that final time.
thm-lie-strang-global-orders-and-subflow.zero: checked|Proof2.1 handles K=0 separately, avoiding division by K; the positive mesh h=T/N is retained in both order estimates.

thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.conclusion: A selected stable local IMEX map on a common tube gives fixed-time order1; it does not prove unconditional root existence or a converse accuracy criterion.
thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.empty: T>0 and N>=1 give an actual grid with both initial and final nodes; the supplied exact and numerical paths witness the common tube.
thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.nonempty-choice: The theorem uses the exact-root map of the already selected local branch; no root outside its certified ball is selected by proof1.1 or2.1.
thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.degenerate: The local supplier controls hLb<=1/2 and admits zero Lipschitz constants; proof2.1 applies its finite stability constants without division by them.
thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.one: checked|For N=1, proof1.1 gives the single local defect Ch^2 and zero initial error; the same global-error supplier used in proof2.1 admits that one-step grid.
thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.endpoints: checked|Proof1.1 sets the initial error to zero and compares every t_n through t_N=T; proof2.1 bounds their maximum, including both endpoints.
thm-imex-euler-global-order-one.zero: checked|The initial-error bound in proof1.1 is exactly zero. Zero step is excluded byT>0,N>=1, and no division by that zero error is used.

thm-imex-euler-algebraic-residual-budget.conclusion: Selected-ball residuals O(h^2), stable exact-root maps and O(h) initial error imply order1; a solver status alone is not a converse residual certificate.
thm-imex-euler-algebraic-residual-budget.empty: The Statement requires N>=1 and an actual candidate in each selected branch ball, so its residual data are an N-term path rather than an empty list.
thm-imex-euler-algebraic-residual-budget.nonempty-choice: Every approximate candidate is supplied by the solver in its selected ball; proof1.1 compares it with the unique exact-root map supplied by the local lemma.
thm-imex-euler-algebraic-residual-budget.degenerate: checked|Proof1.1 uses hLb<=1/2 to obtain the finite factor2. If Cr=0 the algebraic perturbation vanishes and proof2.1 reduces to the exact-root recurrence.
thm-imex-euler-algebraic-residual-budget.endpoints: checked|Proof3.1 retains the Statement's initial boundC0h and bounds the full grid throughT. Its derivative-scaled residual must be multiplied by h before using the update budget.

thm-ars222-additive-order-two-and-tolera.conclusion: The fixed ARS222 method with selected branch roots, common-tube regularity and the two scaled residual budgets has order2; those budgets are sufficient, not a converse characterization.
thm-ars222-additive-order-two-and-tolera.empty: The method has three fixed stages, two selected implicit balls and N>=1 time steps; proof2.1 and3.1 obtain those two roots in sequence.
thm-ars222-additive-order-two-and-tolera.nonempty-choice: Proof2.1 invokes the chosen second-stage root, then proof3.1 the chosen third-stage root; the local branch supplier gives uniqueness in each specified ball.
thm-ars222-additive-order-two-and-tolera.degenerate: checked|Proof1.3 permits r2=r3=0 and then gives zero algebraic stage perturbation. Positive gamma and gamma hLb<=1/2 keep all stage comparison denominators nonzero.
thm-ars222-additive-order-two-and-tolera.endpoints: The final error estimate in proof5.1 includes the supplied initial error and the final nodeT; its scope remains the admitted compact tube and selected stage balls.

prop-ars222-bivariate-stability-region.conclusion: The amplification formula and |R|<=1 region characterize this fixed scalar split test equation, with the implicit pole expressly excluded.
prop-ars222-bivariate-stability-region.empty: This is a scalar two-parameter stability calculation for one specified three-stage tableau, not a selection of modes from an empty matrix spectrum.
prop-ars222-bivariate-stability-region.nonempty-choice: The two stage equations are solved by their explicit scalar denominators in proof1.1; no unspecified eigenvalue or root is chosen.
prop-ars222-bivariate-stability-region.degenerate: checked|Proof1.1 treats the ratios as linear coefficient identities even at y=0, avoiding division by zero initial data. Proof4.1 separately excludes the true pole1-gamma z_b=0.

ex-stiff-explicit-partition-is-unstable.conclusion: The scalar decay example compares explicit amplification with implicit damping; it claims no converse matrix-stability criterion.
ex-stiff-explicit-partition-is-unstable.empty: The Example fixes scalar initial value1 and kappa>0, so the tested trajectory is supplied rather than selected from an empty state set.
ex-stiff-explicit-partition-is-unstable.nonempty-choice: Proof1.1 and1.2 solve the displayed scalar update equations explicitly; no spectrum or multiple-root selection is needed.
ex-stiff-explicit-partition-is-unstable.degenerate: The implicit scalar coefficient1+h kappa is strictly greater than1 by proof1.2, so that branch is nonsingular; zero stiffness is outside kappa>0.
ex-stiff-explicit-partition-is-unstable.one: checked|Proof1.1 gives amplification(1-h kappa)^N for everyN>=1, including the single-step caseN=1.
ex-stiff-explicit-partition-is-unstable.zero: The zero implicit partition b=0 is explicitly used in proof1.1; swapping to a=0 in proof1.2 gives the fully implicit comparison. Neither update divides by a zero field value.

ex-noncommuting-matrices-show-lie-and-st.conclusion: The fixed2x2 nilpotent matrices have nonzero Lie and Strang leading defects at e1; no converse criterion for arbitrary pairs is asserted.
ex-noncommuting-matrices-show-lie-and-st.empty: Both matrices and e1 are explicitly supplied; the two-dimensional coordinate list and the starting vector are nonempty.
ex-noncommuting-matrices-show-lie-and-st.nonempty-choice: Proof1.1 and2.1 multiply the given matrices directly, then proof2.2 and3.1 evaluate their coefficients at the supplied e1.
ex-noncommuting-matrices-show-lie-and-st.one: This is a fixed dimension2 example with a specified first coordinate vector; replacing it by dimension1 changes the counterexample data rather than an omitted parameter branch.
ex-noncommuting-matrices-show-lie-and-st.endpoints: The assertions concern positive small-step asymptotic defects at the supplied vector, not a global finite-time or closed-interval endpoint claim.

ex-finite-matrix-schrodinger-potential-k.conclusion: The given finite Hermitian kinetic/potential matrices have norm-preserving exact subflows yet nonzero splitting defects; no spatial PDE converse is asserted.
ex-finite-matrix-schrodinger-potential-k.empty: The Example supplies two2x2 complex matrices and tests psi=e1; realification has dimension4 and no empty mode selection.
ex-finite-matrix-schrodinger-potential-k.nonempty-choice: Proof1.1 uses the unique global finite matrix flows, and proof3.1 evaluates the explicit bracket coefficients at the specified e1.
ex-finite-matrix-schrodinger-potential-k.one: The construction fixes a two-level complex system, not a one-dimensional parameter family; a single initial coordinate vector is already used in proof3.1.
ex-finite-matrix-schrodinger-potential-k.endpoints: Proof1.1 conserves the norm on every admitted real time interval, and proof3.1 concerns local small-step defects; no unbounded-operator endpoint extension is claimed.

ex-dirichlet-boundary-forcing-strang-ord.conclusion: The specified modal boundary mismatch yields a two-sided h^(5/4) error rate; it is not a converse classification of all inhomogeneous PDE data.
ex-dirichlet-boundary-forcing-strang-ord.empty: The fixed odd-mode forcing has infinitely many nonzero coordinates. Proof4.1 gives at leastH/4 odd modes in[H,2H] forH>=8, ensuring the lower-bound sum is genuinely nonempty.
ex-dirichlet-boundary-forcing-strang-ord.nonempty-choice: Proof1.1 solves every explicit scalar mode and proof4.1 counts the explicit odd integers in a specified interval; no arbitrary mode selection establishes the lower bound.
ex-dirichlet-boundary-forcing-strang-ord.degenerate: Even modal errors are exactly zero by proof2.2, while proof4.1 obtains its strictly positive lower bound from odd modes; zero initial state is explicitly used in proof1.1 and1.2.
ex-dirichlet-boundary-forcing-strang-ord.one: This is an infinite sequence-space example; a single retained mode would satisfy a different finite-dimensional error problem and cannot establish its h^(5/4) lower bound.

ex-reaction-diffusion-ars222-mode-amplif.conclusion: The specified two-cell grid has one growing reaction mode and one damped diffusion mode at h=1/10; no converse nonnormal or PDE stability claim is asserted.
ex-reaction-diffusion-ars222-mode-amplif.empty: Proof1.1 explicitly supplies the two independent vectors(1,1) and(1,-1), so the modal calculation uses a nonempty basis of R2.
ex-reaction-diffusion-ars222-mode-amplif.nonempty-choice: The two vectors in proof1.1 are computed explicitly, and proof2.1 restricts the stage equations to their invariant spans; no unspecified eigenbasis selection is needed.
ex-reaction-diffusion-ars222-mode-amplif.degenerate: checked|The constant diffusion mode has eigenvalue0. Proof2.1 handles its implicit denominator1 and proof3.1 computes R(1/10,0)=221/200, rather than excluding that zero eigenvalue.
ex-reaction-diffusion-ars222-mode-amplif.endpoints: The step is fixed at h=1/10, not an interval parameter; proof4.1 bounds the nonconstant amplification strictly between0 and9/80 using a strictly positive denominator.
